track.name: bankruptcy-law
track.label: Bankruptcy & Insolvency Law
track.summary: The legal mechanics behind every restructuring: the Chapter 11 process end-to-end, the specific Bankruptcy Code sections that actually drive deal terms, creditor priority fights, and how restructuring advisors work alongside counsel.

phases.title: Foundations of Bankruptcy Law
phases.description: Learn what actually happens the moment a company files: the automatic stay that freezes creditor action, how Chapters 7, 11, and 15 differ in practice, and the roles of everyone in the room — debtor's counsel, the UCC, the U.S. Trustee, and the judge.

phases.title: The Chapter 11 Process End-to-End
phases.description: Walk the case from the first-day motions filed within hours of a petition through DIP financing negotiations to the plan of reorganization and disclosure statement that ultimately gets confirmed.

phases.title: Key Legal Mechanisms Every Analyst Should Recognize
phases.description: Go deep on the specific Bankruptcy Code sections that drive deal terms in practice: Section 365 executory contracts and leases, Section 363 asset sales, and Sections 547/548 preference and fraudulent transfer actions.

phases.title: Creditor Rights and Priority Fights
phases.description: Master the absolute priority rule and cramdown in depth, the practical difference between secured and unsecured creditor rights and contractual subordination, and the controversial rules governing executive retention pay in bankruptcy.

phases.title: Cross-Border and Out-of-Court Alternatives
phases.description: Understand how Chapter 15 actually recognizes foreign proceedings, how UK Administration, CVAs, and Schemes of Arrangement compare to Chapter 11, and the legal mechanics of restructuring without ever going to court.

phases.title: Working With Counsel
phases.description: Learn how restructuring advisors and lawyers actually divide the work on a live case, the basics of adversary proceedings and bankruptcy litigation, and how to read a first-day declaration and other real case filings.

topics.title: The Automatic Stay — What Freezes the Moment a Case Is Filed
topics.description: Understand exactly what the automatic stay does and doesn't stop the instant a bankruptcy petition is filed, why it's called 'automatic,' and the statutory exceptions and relief-from-stay process that restructuring professionals need to recognize.

topics.title: Chapters 7, 11, and 15 — Liquidation, Reorganization, and Cross-Border Cases Compared
topics.description: Compare liquidation under Chapter 7, reorganization under Chapter 11, and the ancillary cross-border framework of Chapter 15 — and understand why the choice of chapter shapes everything that follows in a case.

topics.title: Who's in the Room — Debtor's Counsel, the UCC and Its Counsel, the U.S. Trustee, and the Judge
topics.description: Map the actual participants in a Chapter 11 case: debtor's counsel and its fiduciary duties, the Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors and its own counsel, the U.S. Trustee's oversight role, and the bankruptcy judge.

topics.title: First-Day Motions and the First 30 Days of a Case
topics.description: Learn what first-day motions actually ask for — cash management, critical vendors, wages, utilities — and why the first-day hearing sets the tone for the entire case.

topics.title: DIP Financing Agreements — What's Actually in Them and Why Lenders Get Control
topics.description: Go inside an actual DIP credit agreement: budget covenants, milestones, roll-up provisions, priming liens, and the superpriority status that gives DIP lenders outsized leverage over the case.

topics.title: The Plan of Reorganization and Disclosure Statement — From Draft to Confirmation
topics.description: Follow a plan of reorganization from drafting through disclosure statement approval, creditor solicitation, voting, and the confirmation hearing that determines whether a debtor emerges from Chapter 11.

topics.title: Executory Contracts and Unexpired Leases (Section 365) — Assume, Assign, or Reject
topics.description: Understand the debtor's powerful Section 365 right to cherry-pick which contracts and leases to keep, cure and assume, assign to a third party, or reject — and what that means for counterparties.

topics.title: Section 363 Sales — Stalking Horse Bids, Auctions, and Selling Assets Free and Clear
topics.description: Learn how a Section 363 sale lets a debtor sell assets outside a plan, free and clear of liens and claims, through a stalking-horse bid, court-supervised auction, and sale hearing.

topics.title: Preferences and Fraudulent Transfers (Sections 547/548) — Clawing Back Pre-Bankruptcy Payments
topics.description: Understand how a trustee or debtor in possession can claw back payments made shortly before filing under the preference rules of Section 547 and the actual and constructive fraud tests of Section 548.

topics.title: The Absolute Priority Rule and Cramdown, in Depth
topics.description: Go beyond the one-line definition: study how the absolute priority rule actually gets litigated, what 'fair and equitable' requires class by class, the new value exception, and how a plan gets crammed down over an objecting class.

topics.title: Secured vs. Unsecured Creditor Rights and Contractual Subordination
topics.description: Understand what actually separates a secured claim from an unsecured one in a bankruptcy case, and how contractual subordination agreements between creditors get enforced under Section 510.

topics.title: Executive Retention Pay in Bankruptcy — KEIP/KERP Rules and Why They're Controversial
topics.description: Learn the BAPCPA-era rules under Section 503(c) that sharply limit retention bonuses (KERPs) but allow incentive plans tied to difficult-to-reach milestones (KEIPs) — and why courts scrutinize the difference so closely.

topics.title: Chapter 15 — How Cross-Border Insolvency Actually Works
topics.description: Understand how a foreign representative petitions a U.S. court for recognition of a foreign proceeding as 'main' or 'non-main,' and what powers and protections recognition actually confers.

topics.title: UK Administration, CVAs, and Schemes of Arrangement — A Working Comparison to Chapter 11
topics.description: Build a working comparison of the major UK restructuring tools — Administration, Company Voluntary Arrangements, Schemes of Arrangement, and the newer Part 26A Restructuring Plan — against U.S. Chapter 11.

topics.title: Out-of-Court Workouts and Exchange Offers — The Legal Mechanics When You Avoid Court
topics.description: Learn how companies restructure debt entirely outside of bankruptcy court through negotiated workouts and exchange offers, and the securities-law and intercreditor mechanics that make them work.

topics.title: How Restructuring Advisors and Lawyers Actually Divide the Work
topics.description: Understand the practical division of labor on a real case between debtor's counsel, the investment bank or turnaround consultant, and the chief restructuring officer — and how the best teams coordinate.

topics.title: Adversary Proceedings and Bankruptcy Litigation Basics
topics.description: Learn what turns a bankruptcy case into a lawsuit: the categories of disputes that must be filed as adversary proceedings under Rule 7001, and how that litigation track runs alongside the main case.

topics.title: Reading a First-Day Declaration and Other Real Case Filings
topics.description: Read an actual first-day declaration from a major, well-documented Chapter 11 case and learn how to extract the business history, capital structure, and narrative that every other filing in the case builds on.
